dedupe_keys.name: the 2021 tower lake dense array experiment for high resolution microseismicity monitoring during hydraulic fracturing

description: The 2021 Tower Lake Dense Array Experiment for High-Resolution Microseismicity Monitoring During Hydraulic Fracturing is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Ramin M. H. Dokht et al. The rapid expansion of hydraulic fracturing (HF) operations in the Western Canada Sedimentary Basin (WCSB) has significantly altered regional seismicity patterns, leading to an increased frequency of injection-induced earthquakes (IIE). While existing regional networks provide robust monitoring for moderate-magnitude events, they often lack the resolution required to characterize small-magnitude seismicity and detailed rupture processes. Coverage: national (CA); published in 2026. The formats are not stated in the sources read. The paper's page was read, but no repository address could be taken from its machine-readable metadata, so the record links to the article, whose Data Records section names where the data sit. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence of the data is not stated in the sources read (the paper itself is open access). Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support communication-network and digital-infrastructure studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
